messages.subject: Question about displaying summary
parts:
hi :)

i tried to run a cfa. everything worked well until i wanted to display the results with the summary function. here is my script:

dat <- read.spss("Ranalyse.sav",to.data.frame=T)
congeneric.model <- 'WMC =~ DS_pun_b1 + DS_pun_b2 + DS_pun_b3 + DS_pun_b4 + DS_pun_b5'
fit <- cfa(congeneric.model, data=dat, estimator="MLM")
summary(fit, fit.measures=T, standardized=T, rsquare=T)

when creating the fit value, it says it is a "formal class lavaan". when running the summary function the console answers with 

Length Class Mode
       1   lavaan    S4

does anybody have an idea what i'm doing wrong? if i try show(fit) i get the test statistic, so lavaan should be ok. the weird thing is that i remember it working maybe 2 months ago. 

thanks in advance!
philipp

parts:
Could it be that “summary” is masked by a different function with the same name in one of these other loaded packages?  Suppose you detach “lavaan”

 

detach(“package:lavaan”,unload=T)

 

and then reload it, and try summary(fit)—what happens then?  Maybe that would re-associate the name “summary” with lavaan’s version of the function.

--Ed Rigdon

Hm. Can you start over, only load lavaan, and then type

example(cfa)

Do you see the summary() output?

If yes, then one by one, load the other packages that are loaded by your
script. And run summary(fit) every time. Something must be masking
lavaan's summary function. You do not declare a variable called
'summary' in your script, do you?

If all fails, try

lavaan:::summary(fit)

Yves.

On 10/24/2014 09:00 AM, phitho29 wrote:
> Error in get(name, envir = asNamespace(pkg), inherits = FALSE) :
> object 'summary' not found

That is very strange. Two other things you can try:

1) start up RGui.exe (not RStudio); do a fresh install of lavaan, and
try again:

install.packages("lavaan")
library(lavaan)
example(cfa)

2) again, in RGui.exe, reinstall the package by using the 'source' code
(instead of the binary version):

install.packages("lavaan", type = "source")

and look in the output if you see

Creating a generic function for ‘summary’ from package ‘base’ in package
‘lavaan’

Yves.
